title: Parse and build URL query strings
prompt:
The link checker needs to read and rewrite query strings without losing anything, and urllib.parse.parse_qs drops bare keys, so I'd like our own pair of functions in urlbits.py.

parse_query(query: str) -> dict[str, list[str | None]]
- An optional leading "?" is ignored. Split on "&"; empty segments are skipped. Each segment splits on its first "=".
- A segment with no "=" is a bare key and its value is None; "x=" gives the value "".
- Keys and values are decoded: first "+" becomes a space, then %XX escapes (either hex case) are decoded as UTF-8 bytes. A "%" not followed by two hex digits is kept as-is ("100%" stays "100%"). Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD.
- Each key maps to a list of all its values in order; keys are in first-appearance order. parse_query("a=1&flag&a=2") == {"a": ["1", "2"], "flag": [None]}.

build_query(params) -> str
- params maps str keys to a str, None, or a list of str/None. Output has no leading "?". Keys go in mapping order and list values in list order, each as its own pair; an empty list writes nothing for that key.
- None writes the bare key ("flag"), "" writes "key=".
- Keys and values are UTF-8 percent-encoded with uppercase hex; only A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ are left as they are, and a space becomes "+". So {"q": "a b&c"} gives "q=a+b%26c".
- Raise TypeError for any value (or list item) that is not a str or None.

The two should round-trip: parse_query(build_query(p)) == p for any p shaped like parse_query output, and build_query(parse_query(s)) == s when s is already encoded the way build_query encodes and any repeated key's pairs are next to each other.
acceptance: Repeated keys and key order, leading ? and empty segments, bare keys as None vs empty values, first '=' split, + and percent decoding incl. UTF-8, malformed escapes kept, invalid UTF-8 replaced; build_query pairs, None/empty/empty list, exact encoding, TypeError; round trips both ways.
difficulty_rationale: Two functions with several interacting decoding and encoding edge cases and a round-trip requirement.
